answer: Unrepeatable challenge clock. Each identity must, at a random dawn window, solve a fresh compute puzzle whose seed is derived from the previous block hash and a per-identity nonce, then commit the solution before the next cedar checkpoint. Solutions cannot be precomputed, pooled, or replayed because the seed rotates every round. Sybil operators must run real hardware per identity continuously; children mock this with cheap marble tokens, but the puzzle cost scales linearly, so mass identity creation loses money.
